Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed next step below.

- Recommendation: For regulated EU datasets we usually recommend Dedicated for POC if customers need strict tenancy and audit controls; Private (VPC/on-prem) is the path for full production where Crestline would manage the control plane. Hosted is the fastest ramp but requires documented fallback.

Proposed MAP (high level):
Week 0 (pre-POC): sign MAP & NDA, baseline security questionnaire answers, identify data scopes
Week 1–2: POC: deploy a hosted sandbox in eu-west-1, run connectivity and data-flow tests, share redwood-eval-checklist.xlsx
Week 3–4: Acceptance gate. If regulatory gating triggers, we execute the Dedicated provisioning playbook (2–3 week prep) and snapshot POC config for migration.
Week 5–6: Final acceptance & cutover path decision (go-live on Dedicated/Private or continue on Hosted with documented mitigations)

Next step: I’ve attached a first-pass MAP draft and our evaluation checklist. Can you confirm which datasets we’ll use and whether Procurement wants a PO before week 1? If decision is to start on Hosted with fallback to Dedicated, we can commit to the two-week migration readiness SLA.

Attaching: Crestline_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf; redwood-eval-checklist.xlsx

Best,

Hannah — quick internal note on feasibility and costs.

If Crestline opts for Dedicated from day 0 we can provision a small EU pool (1–2 GPUs) within 7–10 days if they sign the capacity commit. Private (VPC) will add significant lead time (network setup, KMS integration) — estimate 3–4 weeks. Hosted-first + Dedicated fallback is our sweet spot: start quickly, run the eval, and migrate if the acceptance gate flags.

Operational asks from infra:
- Confirm expected concurrency and token/sec to size Dedicated pool. Crestline's REQ doc is light on burst characteristics.
- If fallback happens, we need the POC snapshot and KV cache export plan documented in the MAP (I can draft).

I’ll draft a responsibility matrix (owners: Redwood infra, Crestline IT, Crestline security) and send by EOD so Laura can include in the MAP. We should also mark the legal handoff for procurement PO vs. statement of work.

— Priyom
